War is an unreleased collaborative album by American rapper and producer Kanye West and English singer and producer James Blake, conceived in the spring of 2022 following the release of the Stem Player and the exclusive Donda 2 release, and whilst being scrapped in December after West's anti-semitic remarks. This album has also been speculated to have been worked on in 2023. Multiple songs have been released in other eras, such as "Talking" on ¥$'s album, Vultures 1, "Through The High Wire" on James Blake's album,Trying Times, and "This One Here" on Kanye West's album, Bully.
According to James Blake, No I.D. was only there for one session during the album's cycle, and didn't produce most songs. Though it is still confirmed that he was intended to be a credited artist.
Background
In a 2013 interview, West would name James Blake as his favorite artist, and would invite him to collaborate the following year. In a 2016 interview with Pitchfork, Blake would state that he wanted West on his song "Timeless", though the verse would never materialize.
Many songs from War were originally solo James Blake songs that were repurposed for the album. The album was first conceived in April 2022 during sessions for West's album, Donda 2. The album remained unknown to the public until West previewed several songs at a party in London on September 26, 2022. James Blake would confirm his contributions to the album via Twitter. The following day, fellow rapper Pusha T, confirmed he was working with West and No I.D., though it is unknown what songs they working on. The following year, rapper Fat Money, who had collaborated with West on Donda 2, would reveal that West was working on an album with James Blake titled, War.
A copy of the album from October 2022 would leak after multiple unrelated fundraisers in December 2025. West would later state the version of the album that leaked was made from freestyles over James Blake's beats whilst also denying Albe Back's claims of writing for the album.
Many songs from this era would be worked on in other eras, such as West's collaborations with singer Ty Dolla $ign, with "Talking" being released as a single for the duo's debut studio album, Vultures 1. Other tracks such as "All In Love" and "Bobby Digital" would appear on a track list for an early version of Vultures 1, though neither of them would end up releasing on the album. James Blake would release the track "Through the High Wire" on his album Trying Times without vocals from West. "This One Here" released on West's 2026 album, Bully. James Blake would ask to not be credited as a producer for the track.
Track listing
Many copies have been confirmed to exist, and the most major one being the October one, having fully leaked after a series of unrelated fundraisers, being 9 tracks long, which is mostly unfinished, but tracks like "For Once In My Life" and "Quiet" have been confirmed to be about 90% finished, and "What I Would Have Said At Virgil's Funeral" has been confirmed to be finished by James Blake, whether that is the one on the October copy, or another leaked or unknown version.
